90401.text: In the physiological divisions of the atmosphere, what is the zone between 12,000 ft and 50,000 ft called?

90402.text: Which type of hypoxia occurs when the cells cannot use the oxygen available to them, for example in cyanide poisoning or after alcohol?

90403.text: In a case of acute hyperventilation, what is the most effective way to raise the carbon dioxide level in the blood?
options: Breathing deeply into a paper bag
Climbing to a higher altitude immediately

90404.text: What is the name of the manoeuvre in which, with the mouth and nose closed, a forced exhalation is used to equalise the pressure difference between the middle ear and sinuses and the surrounding air?

90405.text: Vaccination against which disease is effective for about ten years and is a standard requirement for international pilots?

90406.text: Which of the following are the fat-soluble vitamins?

90407.text: Approximately how long does it take the rod cells to adapt fully to darkness?

90408.text: What is the name of the condition in which, with ageing, the lens of the eye loses its elasticity and near objects can no longer be seen clearly?

90409.text: A pilot who returns to level flight after a slow, prolonged turn feels banked while actually flying level. Which vestibular illusion is this?

90410.text: In terms of jet lag, flights in which direction are harder to adapt to?
options: Eastward — the day becomes shorter and the body needs more time to adapt
Westward — the body clock shifts forward
Northward — the length of daylight changes

90411.text: According to Hans Selye's General Adaptation Syndrome, what are the three stages of the body's response to stress, in order?

90412.text: What is the name of the rule that prohibits non-essential conversation during critical phases of flight such as take-off, descent and landing?

90413.text: In the FORDEC decision-making model, what does the letter 'R' stand for?

90414.text: What is the top level of Maslow's hierarchy of needs?
